comparability_warning: Two numbers may only be reported side by side if they share dataset AND same SA normalisation scale. The LigandDiff 0.68-0.80 band uses an UNSTATED scale.

gao_coley_parameters.calibrated_against: Population mean and standard deviation of Ertl SA across the Enamine REAL / ZINC15-clean-3 lead-like library (Gao & Coley 2020, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 60, 5714-5723, DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00174). NOT derived from tmQM or any organometallic corpus.

gaps.note: All gaps are arithmetic. The 'sa_norm_gao_coley_generated_minus_real' value is informative only as a ratio (real / generated), because both numbers are themselves the exp of -delta/sigma and the underlying raw delta dominates. See 'how_to_read' for the recommended reporting form.

how_to_read: On the linear hack, generated 0.36 vs real 0.50 (gap 0.14 open) -- this is what the repo has always quoted. On Gao-Coley, generated ~0.002 vs real ~0.015 (a ~7x ratio, not a comparable 0.14 -- the two scales are different functions and 0.14 on one is not the same physical claim as 0.14 on the other). The LigandDiff 0.68 band is from a paper whose SA normalisation is UNSTATED; do not cite it side-by-side with either scale until verified.

linear_hack_parameters.what_is_wrong_with_it: Linear rescaling of the Ertl range [1,10] ignores the calibrated Gaussian-shaped difficulty profile. A SA of 4 (moderate) and a SA of 6 (hard) get mapped to 0.6 and 0.4 respectively, but Ertl's own rating of these is not linearly proportional.

literature_comparison.citation: Jin H, Merz KM Jr. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20(10), 4377-4384. DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.4c00232.
literature_comparison.comparability_with_this_repo_verdict: NOT VERIFIED. LigandDiff does not cite Gao & Coley, Brown (GuacaMol), or any other normalised-SA paper. Until LigandDiff's implementation is read, LigandDiff's 0.68-0.80 band is incomparable to BOTH our scales: if their scale equals the Gao-Coley scale the gap is computed below; if their scale equals the linear hack the gap is the same shape at a different magnitude.

Computing the LigandDiff scale for our cohort until the paper's normalisation is identified.
Replacing the Linear hack repo-wide -- that is a downstream decision; this script only computes both numbers.
purpose: Score the SAME two cohorts (generated n=66 and real_tmQM six-metal n=31150) on TWO different SA normalisation scales. The two scales are NOT comparable to each other and NOT comparable to LigandDiff's 0.68-0.80 band unless LigandDiff's own normalisation is verified.

corrections_2026_10_12_evening.summary: The function name gao_coley_sa_norm and the docstring it carried for the entire Round-1/2 record misdescribed the formula shape as a 'half-Gaussian' / 'Gao-Coley normalisation' when it is in fact an asymmetric exponential decay. The numbers in this JSON are unchanged (the formula is what it has always been); only the prose naming was wrong. Corrected 2026-10-12 by adversarial review.
what_was_wrong: Function name 'gao_coley_sa_norm' implied the canonical Gao-Coley form. The canonical form is exp(-0.5*((max(sa,mu)-mu)/sigma)^2) (MOMO-master/losses.py::normalize_sa, a symmetric Gaussian clamped at mu). The function in this repo computes exp(-(sa-mu)/sigma), an asymmetric exponential decay, NOT a Gaussian, NOT a half-Gaussian, NOT a clamped form.

Docstring called the formula 'asymmetric half-Gaussian' -- it is an asymmetric exponential, not a half-Gaussian. A half-Gaussian would still have a squared argument (exp(-0.5*((x-mu)/sigma)^2) for x>=mu and 1 for x<mu).
Module constants GAO_COLEY_MU=2.230044, GAO_COLEY_SIGMA=0.6526308 are corroborated against MOMO-master/losses.py but their provenance to the indexed Gao-Coley 2020 paper itself is UNVERIFIED.
what_was_landed_2026_10_12: Renamed function (with backward-compat alias): the corrected, accurate name is molmetal.adapters.sa_gao_coley.asymmetric_exponential_sa. The legacy name gao_coley_sa_norm is kept as a forward (same callable, not a re-implementation) so existing callers and the smoke test in this JSON's n=66 integration check do not break.

Updated the module docstring to describe the formula accurately: 'asymmetric exponential decay, not a Gaussian, not a half-Gaussian', with an explicit note that the canonical MOMO form differs by a factor of 1.7e6 at sa_raw=6.44.

Added two new red-check tests in molmetal/tests/test_sa_gao_coley.py: (1) test_corrected_name_exposed_and_alias_works pins the rename and verifies the alias is the same callable; (2) test_module_docstring_does_not_call_formula_half_gaussian checks the docstring does not reintroduce the 'half-Gaussian' framing in a non-negation, non-quoted context. Both go red if reverted. Verified by revert+confirm-red+restore on 2026-10-12.

Renamed test_formula_is_asymmetric_half_gaussian_not_symmetric -> test_formula_is_asymmetric_exponential_not_symmetric_gaussian, with the formula-identity assertion unchanged (still pins the asymmetric-exp value, not the symmetric Gaussian value).
what_is_NOT_changed: All numeric values in this JSON (generated 0.00251 / 0.00163 mean+median; real 0.03025 / 0.01850; LigandDiff gap -0.6775; linear-hack 0.36 / 0.50; etc.) are unchanged. The function computed the same formula before and after the rename.
The LigandDiff comparability verdict (NOT VERIFIED) is unchanged. The renaming of the function does not help with the literature comparison: the unstated LigandDiff scale remains unstated.
corrections_2026_10_12_evening.downstream_decision_recorded_not_acted_o: Rerunning the cohort through the canonical MOMO form (symmetric Gaussian clamped at mu) would change every reported value by a factor up to ~1e6 and is a downstream decision. The misnomer has been corrected and a test now pins the new prose; the published numbers stand as-is. Any paper that cites this JSON should add a one-line note: 'Gao-Coley parameters, asymmetric-exponential form; the canonical MOMO form differs by a factor up to ~1e6 at this cohort's SA range'.
